name: Recard the Gathering
note: The rules below are written out IN FULL on purpose (US-127/D151). Recard's own rules reference gives this game three sentences, which assume conventions they never state. Those conventions were researched and written down here, once, so that a person can argue with them and play never depends on what a model happens to remember.

rules.goal: Each player starts at 20 life. Reduce the opponent to 0.
rules.turn_sequence: A turn goes: untap everything you control, draw one card, then a main phase, then combat, then the turn ends. You may cast spells and play a land during your main phase.
rules.land_drop: You may put at most one land onto the battlefield per turn, from your hand, and only during your own main phase.
rules.mana: Tap an untapped land you control to pay for a spell. A spell's cost must be paid in full before it is cast; a spell you cannot pay for cannot be cast.
rules.casting: A spell you cast goes on the shared Stack. The Stack resolves top-down once both players are done responding. A creature that resolves arrives on your battlefield.
rules.summoning_sickness: A creature cannot attack, and cannot be tapped for an effect, unless it has been on your battlefield since the beginning of your most recent turn. A creature that arrived this turn cannot attack this turn.
rules.attacking: Only untapped creatures without summoning sickness may attack. Attacking taps the creature. You choose which of your creatures attack; you attack the opponent, not their creatures.
rules.blocking: The defending player may block each attacking creature with one untapped creature they control. A tapped creature cannot block. A creature that arrived this turn may still block.
rules.damage: An attacking creature blocked by a creature deals its power to that blocker and takes the blocker's power in return; a creature that has taken damage equal to or greater than its toughness dies and goes to its owner's graveyard. An unblocked attacker deals its power to the defending player, who loses that much life.
rules.priority: Either player may respond while something is on the Stack. Recard does not track priority: players say what they are doing, and the table settles it.
rules.seating: Turns pass clockwise. The player counter-clockwise from me is the one whose turn it currently is, if anyone's.
rules.no_mechanical_signal: Nothing about the board alone proves a turn has ended - a player may hold mana untapped for instants, and may choose not to attack at all. Work out what happened from the board as it stands now and what was said, in order.

one_land_per_turn.instructions: The move puts a land onto the battlefield. Given `rules.land_drop`, `turn.land_played` and `turn.is_mine`, is that allowed right now?

can_pay_for_it.instructions: Given `rules.mana` and `me.untapped_lands`, can this spell's cost in `proposed.cost` be paid in full right now?

creature_can_attack.instructions: Given `rules.attacking` and `rules.summoning_sickness`, may the creature in `proposed.card` attack this turn, considering `proposed.arrived_this_turn` and `proposed.tapped`?

block_is_legal.instructions: Given `rules.blocking`, may the creature in `proposed.card` block the attacker named in `turn.attackers`, considering `proposed.tapped`?

timing_is_right.instructions: Given `rules.turn_sequence`, `rules.priority`, `turn.is_mine` and `turn.phase`, is this the right moment for the move in `proposed.what`?

attack_phase_complete.instructions: Given `rules.no_mechanical_signal`, the board in `me` and `opponent`, and `table_talk` in order, IF the counter-clockwise player declared an attack this turn, has it been resolved? Answer yes if no attack was declared at all - there is nothing pending.

their_turn_is_over.instructions: Given `rules.seating`, `rules.no_mechanical_signal`, the board in `me` and `opponent`, `table_talk` in order, and the read on `attack_phase_complete` - has the counter-clockwise player's turn ended? Judge only from the board and what was said - never guess about something already visible.

step.instructions: It is my move in Recard the Gathering. Given `rules.goal`, what I hold in `me` and what the opponent has in `opponent`, which of these should I do next? Passing is always allowed.

criteria.untap_all: Untap everything I control, which starts my turn.
criteria.draw: Draw a card for the turn.
criteria.play_land: Put a land from my hand onto the battlefield - the one land I get this turn.
criteria.cast: Cast this spell from my hand, tapping lands to pay for it.
criteria.block: Block the attacking creature with this one.
criteria.take_damage: Take the damage from what got through, off my life total.
criteria.pass: Do nothing further and let the table move on.
